forces.title: Payments value migrating to invisible software control layer
forces.description: Global payments are undergoing a structural shift where value is relocating from visible front-end checkouts to an invisible back-end 'control layer' of software. This layer encompasses trust, machine identity, consent engines, and dynamic routing protocols for autonomous software agents. This change moves revenue away from traditional transaction interfaces, necessitating a re-evaluation of where application software creates value within the payment ecosystem.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Agentic AI reshaping payments economics and value capture
forces.description: Agentic artificial intelligence, an advanced form of application software, is poised to reshape payments economics by enabling autonomous software agents to optimize financial activities for consumers and corporations. These agents can manage account yields, dynamically route transactions for cost savings, and automate purchasing decisions. This shift implies that application software providing agentic capabilities will become central to capturing value, challenging existing business models in the financial sector.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Emergence of new infrastructure products for agentic payments
forces.description: Agentic payments introduce new challenges that create opportunities for innovative application software products. These include cryptographic credentials for agents, standardized mandate and consent management protocols, granular risk controls and policy guardrails, dedicated agent wallets, and transaction protection frameworks for delegated flows. These new services generate recurring per-mandate fees, per-call API pricing, and risk-bearing premiums, offering a more defensible and lucrative margin structure than traditional transaction processing for application software providers.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: B2B commerce drives early adoption of agentic software
forces.description: Business-to-business (B2B) commerce is leading the adoption of autonomous software agents faster than consumer commerce. Traditional e-procurement is evolving into agent-driven processes for sourcing, bid evaluation, negotiation, and settlement, guided by institutional criteria. The structured, mandate-governed, and machine-readable nature of B2B flows makes this sector a larger and earlier-moving market for advanced application software solutions leveraging agentic AI, indicating significant near-term growth.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Strong venture capital funding for European AI applications
forces.description: European AI application layer start-ups are experiencing a significant surge in venture capital funding, with H1 2026 funding reaching 44% of US levels, a substantial increase from 11% in 2018. This growth, particularly pronounced in vertical AI applications (67% of US levels), reflects rising investor confidence and capital availability. This positive funding environment acts as a tailwind, enabling European application software companies to innovate, scale, and compete globally.
forces.source_title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity

forces.title: Reversing AI talent migration bolsters European software development
forces.description: Europe is benefiting from a net inflow of AI professionals from the United States, observed for the first time in 2025. Countries like Germany and the United Kingdom are emerging as significant AI talent hubs, complemented by narrowing transatlantic pay gaps for top-tier roles. This enhanced availability of skilled AI professionals, coupled with strong university spinout ecosystems, provides a crucial tailwind for the development and scaling of sophisticated application software solutions across the region.
forces.source_title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity

forces.title: Increased corporate and state-backed investment in AI applications
forces.description: European AI application venture capital deals are increasingly supported by corporate and state-backed investors. Corporate investor participation in these deals grew to 39% of US levels in H1 2026, while state-backed funds accounted for 24% of the region's AI application VC deal value. Initiatives like the EU AI Champions Initiative, with €1 billion in co-investments, and the €200 billion InvestAI program, provide critical strategic capital and partnerships, boosting application software development and deployment.
forces.source_title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity

forces.title: Growing US investor interest in European AI application software
forces.description: US investors are significantly contributing to Europe's AI application layer momentum, with their participation in European AI application deals rising from 49% in 2018 to 84% in 2026. This influx of capital, particularly concentrated in Europe's vertical AI layer, empowers European application software companies. It allows them to access crucial funding needed to scale their domain-specific and compliance-native solutions, fostering global competitiveness and accelerating innovation.
forces.source_title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity

forces.title: AI and automation boosting business process optimization
forces.description: European truck OEMs and suppliers are leveraging agentic and physical AI to re-engineer and automate core, cross-functional business processes. This strategic integration of application software capabilities leads to significantly shortened development cycles, enhanced sales and aftersales performance, and substantial cost optimizations in critical areas like planning, production, and procurement. This driver creates significant opportunities for application software providers specializing in industrial and logistics sectors.
forces.source_title: Competing in the fast lane—the future of Europe’s truck industry

forces.title: AI tech stack competitive focus shifts to application layer
forces.description: The competitive landscape in the AI tech stack is structurally shifting, with increasing enterprise adoption moving beyond AI experimentation to the redesign of legacy business processes. This change concentrates competitive focus on the application layer: software engineered to understand specific workflows, integrate seamlessly with existing enterprise systems, and automate tasks in complex operational environments. This signifies a profound reorientation, making application software a primary battleground for AI value creation.
forces.source_title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity

viewpoints.title: Software and workflow layers capture increasing gross profit in payments
viewpoints.description: McKinsey analysis reveals a structural shift in global payments, with gross profit expansion increasingly concentrating in the software and workflow layers surrounding transactions. Software-led acquirers and vertical SaaS platforms now generate 40-60% of their gross profit from embedded payments, value-added services, and software subscriptions, achieving margins up to 80% versus 20-30% for core processing. Public markets reward this software-led distribution and deep workflow integration with significant valuation premiums. This signifies application software's growing central role in value capture.
viewpoints.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

viewpoints.title: Europe well-positioned for AI application layer competitiveness
viewpoints.description: Europe's technology ecosystem is entering a new era of AI maturity, shifting competitive focus towards the application layer of the AI tech stack. This layer, requiring deep understanding of specific workflows and integration into complex enterprise systems, aligns well with Europe's established industrial expertise, regulatory rigor, and diverse markets. McKinsey research suggests this shift disproportionately benefits Europe's technological competitiveness, making it a strong region for application software development.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity

viewpoints.title: Vertical AI application funding converging sharply with US levels in Europe
viewpoints.description: European start-ups specializing in vertical AI applications are rapidly closing the funding gap with their US counterparts, demonstrating the sharpest convergence across the entire tech stack. In the first half of 2026, venture capital funding for these firms reached 67% of US levels, a significant increase from 9% in 2018. This trend highlights growing investor confidence and the emergence of European AI leaders in specialized application software solutions for complex environments.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity

viewpoints.title: Application software to remain vital despite foundational AI model growth
viewpoints.description: Despite substantial investment in foundational large language models (LLMs), AI applications are expected to remain a distinct and strong segment. Applications demand a different talent profile, focusing on deployment engineers and domain experts embedded with customers to provide workflow depth. Historical technological shifts, such as the internet/cloud (70%) and mobile (85%) cycles, show application companies consistently capturing the largest share of ecosystem value, supporting this long-term outlook.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity

viewpoints.title: Agentic treasury management emerges as early commercial opportunity
viewpoints.description: Agentic treasury management is identified as one of the earliest and most promising commercial opportunities stemming from autonomous software agents. Venture-backed platforms, including companies like Kyriba and Trovata, are actively developing and deploying autonomous treasury agents. These solutions manage cash positioning, working capital forecasting, and payment execution for businesses, dynamically sourcing liquidity and rails. This signals a significant and immediate growth area for specialized application software.
viewpoints.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

viewpoints.title: Deep ERP integration crucial for accelerating agentic AI adoption
viewpoints.description: The advancement of agentic AI execution is significantly driven by workflow structures already featuring mandates, ERP integrations, and robust system-to-system data exchange. Flows such as procure-to-pay and corporate FX optimization are progressing rapidly towards full agentic stages by 2030, unlike discretionary human-validated processes. This indicates that existing enterprise application software, particularly ERP systems, will play a critical role in facilitating and accelerating the adoption and value realization of new agentic AI capabilities.
viewpoints.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

viewpoints.title: European vertical AI thrives by navigating industry complexities
viewpoints.description: European AI start-ups demonstrate competitive strength by focusing on specialized, compliance-ready solutions for deeply entrenched and highly regulated sectors. Approximately 94% of European vertical AI investment targets industrial, defense, legal, healthcare, and financial services. This strategic focus enables these application software providers to develop robust solutions tailored to complex environments, making them less susceptible to competition from broader, general-purpose AI platforms.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity
